paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is a LOT of names, and I want you to hear what all those names are saying. God gave Judah a real place, with real borders, down to every town and village. Nothing is vague here. Joshua 15:20 sums it up: "This is the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Judah." When God hands something over, He hands it over on purpose, and He doesn't leave anyone guessing.

Now look at Caleb. Joshua gave him Hebron "According to the LORD's command to him" (Joshua 15:13), and then Caleb went and drove out the three sons of Anak who were living there (Joshua 15:14). The gift was real, and Caleb still got up and did his part. I think that's the lesson for you and me. God's promises are solid, and we walk into them with our feet moving. Then Acsah asks her father, "Give me a blessing," and she gets springs of water (Joshua 15:19). She asked, and she got MORE than land. Friend, what's stopping you from asking?

The chapter ends with a hard note. Judah "could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem," and the writer says that "to this day the Jebusites live there among the descendants of Judah" (Joshua 15:63). I think that line stings a little. The land was given, but not every part was taken. I'm telling you, friend, God's gift is bigger than our follow-through, so let's keep our ovens ready and keep pressing on. The story isn't over.
